name: Nebuchadnezzar
bio: Nebuchadnezzar, king of Babylon, made Jehoiakim, king of Judah, his vassal; when Jehoiakim later rebelled, the LORD sent raiding bands against Judah as judgment for Manasseh's old sins. After Jehoiakim's death, Nebuchadnezzar's forces besieged Jerusalem under the new king Jehoiachin, who surrendered himself, his mother, and his officials in the eighth year of Nebuchadnezzar's reign. Nebuchadnezzar stripped the temple and palace of their treasures, destroyed the gold vessels Solomon had made, and deported Jehoiachin, the royal family, the officials, the craftsmen, and thousands of Jerusalem's leading citizens to Babylon, leaving only the poorest people in the land. He then installed Mattaniah, Jehoiachin's uncle, as king, renaming him Zedekiah (2 Kings 24:1-17). Zedekiah's eventual rebellion against Nebuchadnezzar, and Babylon's final destruction of Jerusalem, are told in detail in the chapters ahead.
